documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute COPD Exacerbation with Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 04:10, HD1
CC: shortness of breath x 3 days, worse tonight
HPI:
69 y/o male with severe COPD (GOLD D, FEV1 34% predicted 8 mo ago) presents with 3 days progressive dyspnea, productive cough, yellow-green sputum.
Wheeze poorly responsive to home MDI; used albuterol MDI q2h at home overnight without relief.
Denies fever, chest pain, orthopnea, hemoptysis, leg swelling. No sick contacts. Grandson with URI last week.
Uses home oxygen 2L continuously; required 5L NC in the ED to maintain target saturation.
Arrived by EMS at 01:25. SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
ED COURSE:
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing.
Azithromycin 500 mg IV given 03:45. Mag sulfate 2 g IV 03:50.
PMH:
COPD, 2 prior admissions in past 12 mo, one requiring BiPAP
Former smoker, 50 pack-yr, quit 4 yrs ago
HTN
Type 2 DM, last A1c 7.4
Chronic hypercapnia at baseline (PaCO2 ~50)
OSA - does not tolerate home CPAP
PSH: inguinal hernia repair, remote
HOME MEDS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
ASA 81 mg daily
ALLERGIES: penicillin - rash
SOCIAL: lives with wife in single-level home. Daughter nearby. Ambulates with cane, limited to ~20 feet by dyspnea. No alcohol. No vaping.
FHx: father emphysema, mother CAD
ROS: positive for dyspnea, cough, sputum, fatigue. Negative for fever, chills, dysuria, rash, syncope.
EXAM:
T 37.1, HR 108 sinus tach, BP 148/86, RR 32, SpO2 92% on BiPAP 14/6
Gen: ill-appearing, anxious, diaphoretic
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
HEENT: BiPAP mask in place, oral mucosa dry, no JVD appreciated
Lungs: barrel chest, diffuse expiratory wheeze both fields, prolonged expiratory phase, poor air movement at bases, no focal crackles
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no S3
Abd: soft, nontender, nondistended, BS present
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness, nails with mild clubbing
Neuro: alert, follows commands, oriented x3, no asterixis, no tremor
Skin: warm, no rash
LABS/IMAGING:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 14.6, Plt 244
Na 137, K 4.1, Cl 96, HCO3 31, BUN 19, Cr 0.94, glucose 188
Lactate 1.6. Trop <0.02 x1. BNP 84.
Resp viral panel pending. Blood cx x2 drawn 03:40. Sputum cx sent.
CXR portable: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no infiltrate, no effusion, no pneumothorax
ECG: sinus tach 110, no acute ischemic change, low voltage
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Acute COPD exacerbation with acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure - likely viral trigger. Continue NIV, titrate to WOB and pH. Repeat gas in 4h.
2. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours. Plan taper to PO prednisone once WOB improves.
3. Abx: azithromycin IV, day 1 of 5 (PCN allergy - avoid beta-lactam).
4. Scheduled duoneb q4h with q2h prn, RT to assess.
5. DM: hold metformin, SSI q6h given steroid burden, check glucose q6h.
6. HTN: continue lisinopril. 7. VTE ppx: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily.
8. Telemetry, strict I/O, HOB elevated. Code status: full, confirmed with pt and wife.
Dispo: step-down unit. Attending notified; will round at 07:00.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 AM - COPD Exacerbation
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD2, 07:20
SUBJECTIVE: Pt reports breathing somewhat easier this morning. Tolerating mask better. Slept in 2h stretches. Cough still productive, sputum thinner.
Remained on BiPAP 14/6 continuously for 9 hours, then transitioned to 5L NC at 12:30 HD1; plan nocturnally on night 2.
Overnight: no fevers, no chest pain. One prn duoneb at 04:00 for wheeze.
OBJECTIVE:
Weight 81.2 kg, up 0.4 kg. I/O 1450/1200.
Gen: more comfortable, sitting upright, speaking in full sentences now
Lungs: expiratory wheeze still diffuse but improved air movement, no crackles
CV: RRR, no murmur. Abd soft. Ext no edema.
Neuro: alert, oriented, no asterixis
Repeat ABG 06:40: pH 7.35, PaCO2 56, PaO2 66 on 4L
Labs: WBC 11.4, Hgb 14.1, K 3.7, HCO3 30, Cr 0.88
Glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale; added scheduled glargine 10 units nightly.
Blood cx no growth to date. Resp viral panel positive for rhinovirus.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation, improving. Continue nocturnal BiPAP tonight. Wean O2 toward home 2L as tolerated, target SpO2 88-92%.
2. Continue methylprednisolone 40 mg IV q8h today; plan to switch to prednisone 40 mg PO in AM if trajectory holds.
3. Continue azithromycin, day 2 of 5.
4. Duoneb q4h scheduled, q2h prn. RT to review MDI technique.
5. Steroid hyperglycemia - KCl 40 mEq PO x1 for K 3.7, continue SSI q6h, glargine added, monitor q6h glucose.
6. PT eval ordered for mobility and ambulatory sat check.
7. Continue enoxaparin ppx. Encourage incentive spirometer q1h while awake.
Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside. Attending agrees.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5 - COPD Exacerbation, Weaning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE HD5, 08:05
SUBJECTIVE: Pt feels markedly better. Walked to hallway and back with RN yesterday afternoon. Denies dyspnea at rest. Cough occasional, sputum clear.
Off BiPAP since night 2 - no nocturnal NIV required nights 3, 4. Slept well on 2L NC.
OBJECTIVE:
T 36.8, HR 82, BP 130/76, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 2L NC (home baseline)
Ambulatory sat check with PT: 88% on 2L at 150 feet, recovered to 93% after 1 min rest.
Gen: comfortable, no distress, speaking in full sentences
Lungs: mild scattered end-expiratory wheeze, good air movement throughout, no crackles
CV: RRR. Abd benign. Ext: no edema.
No accessory muscle use today.
Labs: WBC 8.1, Hgb 13.8, Na 139, K 4.2, HCO3 29, Cr 0.90
Glucose trend 162, 188, 174, 155 over past 24h on prednisone 40 mg PO daily
Sputum cx: normal respiratory flora. Blood cx x2 negative, final.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation, resolving. Back to home oxygen 2L requirement. Completed azithromycin 5-day course last night.
2. Prednisone 40 mg PO daily - total 5-day course, last dose tomorrow, no taper needed given short course.
3. Hyperglycemia improving as steroid tapers off - continue SSI, reduce glargine to 6 units, restart metformin 500 mg BID today.
4. Continue tiotropium, budesonide-formoterol, prn albuterol. MDI technique reviewed by RT, pt demonstrated correctly x2.
5. PT: ambulating 150 feet with cane, cleared for home with daughter support.
6. Pulm rehab referral placed. Smoking cessation reinforced - remains abstinent 4 yrs.
7. Anticipate discharge HD6 if overnight sats stable on 2L.
Home O2 equipment confirmed functional by wife. Action plan and rescue pack to be reviewed at discharge.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation with Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD6 at 13:40. LOS 6 days.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute COPD exacerbation with acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure
2. Rhinovirus upper respiratory infection
3. Steroid-induced hyperglycemia, type 2 DM
4. HTN
BRIEF COURSE:
69 y/o male with severe COPD on home O2 presented with 3 days of progressive dyspnea and productive cough. SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
On arrival there was visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Three albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers given in the ED between 01:40 and 03:00 plus methylprednisolone 125 mg IV; persistent diffuse wheeze and dyspnea at rest afterward.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
Treated with IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours; glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale. Managed with SSI and short-course glargine.
Azithromycin IV then PO, 5-day course completed HD4. Blood and sputum cultures negative. CXR without infiltrate.
Uses home oxygen 2L continuously; required 5L NC in the ED to maintain target saturation. By HD5 back to 2L NC baseline with SpO2 92% at rest.
Steroids converted to prednisone 40 mg PO on HD3, last dose HD6, no taper.
DISCHARGE EXAM: T 36.7, HR 78, BP 128/74, RR 16, SpO2 93% on 2L NC. Mild scattered wheeze, good air movement, no accessory muscle use. Ambulates 200 feet with cane.
DISCHARGE LABS: WBC 7.4, Hgb 13.9, K 4.3, HCO3 28, Cr 0.89, glucose 141
DISCHARGE MEDS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID with spacer
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn wheeze
Metformin 1000 mg BID (resumed full dose)
Lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, ASA 81 mg daily
Glargine and sliding scale insulin STOPPED at discharge
Home oxygen 2L continuous by nasal cannula, target SpO2 88-92%
INSTRUCTIONS: Use spacer with every inhaler dose. Do not exceed 2L without instruction. Daily glucose checks AM x 1 week.
Return for increasing dyspnea, sputum color change, fever, confusion, or sats persistently below 88 on 2L.
FOLLOW-UP: pulmonary clinic in 7-10 days with spirometry; primary care in 2 weeks for glucose and BP; pulmonary rehab intake call pending.
Discharged home with wife; daughter to stay first 3 nights. Instructions reviewed with pt and daughter, teach-back completed.
